clue.text: First mate biting lip

indicators.note: a mouth biting something has it held between its jaws, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend
the rim of a cup is its lip, its edge

explanation.surface: A first mate on a ship chewing his lip anxiously.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means original or earliest, the first in a sequence of development.

clue.text: Galloped hard, circling Charlie's farm

indicators.note: to circle something is to go round it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: galloped means ran
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie's horse galloped hard round the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one raising cattle in North America.

clue.text: Otherwise expressed, thin gloom

indicators.note: expressed otherwise means said a different way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Putting a faint darkness into other words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Otherwise expressed' rearranges THINGLOOM, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonlight is the pale, weak light that relieves night's darkness only thinly.

clue.text: Introduction of Romance language round Spain

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: Ladin is a Romance language of the Dolomites in northern Italy
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: An introduction to a Romance language covering Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead-in is an introductory passage or remark that opens something.

clue.text: Finest daily record (with front cover missing) — old book of animals

parts.note: the finest is the best

indicators.note: the front cover of a book is its first page, so the opening letter of the record is lost

parts.note: a diary is a record kept day by day

explanation.surface: A dog-eared copy of the best journal, its cover torn off, turns out to be a medieval animal book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with front cover missing' drops the D from DIARY, leaving IARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestiary is a medieval illustrated treatise describing real and fabulous creatures, often with moral lessons.

clue.text: Rearranged Banbury's leading fund-raising event

indicators.note: rearranged means put into a different order, signalling a mix of letters

explanation.surface: Banbury's top charity event has been reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: A bring-and-buy sale is a British charity sale where people donate items and buy others'. Banbury is an English market town.
explanation.definitionFit: Such sales are held by churches and schools to raise money for good causes.

clue.text: Tops and just one t-shirt for starters

parts.note: single means just one

indicators.note: starters are the openings, so the initial letters are taken

explanation.surface: Tops, plus one T-shirt to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' takes the T and S that start the two parts of t-shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Singlets are sleeveless vests or tops worn under shirts or for sport.

clue.text: Small hotel's appeal isn't it for some

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel or pub
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A small hotel's charm, isn't it, for some guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Innit is a colloquial contraction used by some speakers, standing for isn't it in tag questions.

clue.text: Port gives mother a bad character

parts.note: a rotter is a cad, a nasty person
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: Fortified wine gives a mother a bad reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the drink; it is the harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam in the Netherlands is one of Europe's largest seaports.

clue.text: Novelty tavern gets good cheer

parts.note: an inn is a tavern, a pub
an ovation is a round of cheering and applause

explanation.surface: A pub with some new attraction draws hearty cheers from its regulars.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovation is something newly introduced, a novelty or fresh idea.

clue.text: Barking heads

definitions.meaning: barking is British slang for mad
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Dogs' heads barking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are informal: crazy behaviour, and the skull as a hard casing like a nutshell.

clue.text: Bob and Sir Rowland in prison. Not half!

indicators.note: one name is placed inside the other here, as an inmate sits in a cell
only half of the prison's doubled name is kept, the other half dropped

parts.note: Sing Sing is a famous prison in New York State
Sir Rowland Hill founded the penny post in Britain

explanation.surface: Bob and Sir Rowland locked up together, with an emphatic 'Not half!' of agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' keeps one half of the prison's doubled name. A bob was British slang for a shilling, the pre-decimal coin worth twelve pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob was the everyday British nickname for the old twelve-penny coin.

clue.text: Scraps that could make one brood

definitions.meaning: scraps of rubbish left lying about
a single brood of young animals born together

explanation.surface: Rubbish that might make someone sulk and brood.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter means both discarded waste and a set of offspring born at one time to an animal.

clue.text: Tennis player of no interest dropping in

indicators.note: dropping a word means letting it fall out of the longer one

parts.note: something of no interest is boring

explanation.surface: A tennis player too dull to watch keeps dropping in uninvited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping in' looks like a social visit, but 'dropping' removes the IN from BORING.
explanation.definitionFit: Björn Borg is the Swedish champion who won five Wimbledon titles in a row.

clue.text: Exaggerates deliveries per hour

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six deliveries by one bowler
a rate is an amount per unit of time, such as per hour

explanation.surface: A cricket statistic for how many overs are bowled each hour.
explanation.walkthrough: Over rate is the cricket measure of overs bowled per hour.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrate is to value something too highly, overstating its worth.

clue.text: Places to keep records and money after apartment is secured

indicators.note: something secured is held fast, here enclosed within the other piece

parts.note: notes are paper money, banknotes
a pad is slang for a flat or apartment

explanation.surface: Where to keep your files and your cash once the flat is locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Notepads are pads of paper where people jot down and keep written records.

clue.text: Who comes to aid camper when injured?

definitions.text: Who comes to aid camper when injured?

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking who helps a camper who gets hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges AIDCAMPER; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramedic is a trained medical responder who attends emergencies.

clue.text: Smiley caught feeling outside

indicators.note: the longer word sits outside, wrapping round the letter

parts.note: an emotion is a feeling
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A smiling person caught with feeling all over their face.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley is a face symbol typed in messages, a kind of emoticon.

clue.text: Invited crowd to mill around bar? Not me!

indicators.note: people who mill around move about aimlessly, so these letters jostle into a new order

explanation.surface: A crowd asked to hang around the pub, with someone pointedly declining to join.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mill around' rearranges BARNOTME; the question mark flags the misleading picture of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent-a-mob is a crowd hired or invited to swell a protest or demonstration.

clue.text: Cut card, first to be discarded

indicators.note: the opening letter is thrown away, as a card is discarded in a game

parts.note: a trump is a card of the suit ranking above the others

explanation.surface: Instructions in a card game: cut the deck, then discard the first card.
explanation.definitionFit: Rump is a cut of beef taken from the animal's hindquarters.

clue.text: Demolishing wings, smash large building stone

indicators.note: the wings are the outer parts of the phrase, which are knocked away

explanation.surface: A wrecking crew smashes the wings of a large stone building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demolishing wings' strips SM and GE from the ends of SMASHLARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is dressed, squared masonry stone used to face buildings.

clue.text: English maestro not getting second, or silver

indicators.note: not getting something means going without it, so a letter is left out

parts.note: Sir Malcolm Sargent was a celebrated English conductor

explanation.surface: An English musician fails to finish second and takes silver anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not getting' drops the S from SARGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Argent is the heraldic term for the tincture silver.

clue.text: Seeing bears regularly going to mountain

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Spotting bears now and then on the way up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eiger is a famous Alpine peak in Switzerland, known for its north face.

clue.text: Greeting Middle Easterner in park

parts.note: yo is an informal greeting
a Semite is a member of the peoples of the Middle East, such as Arabs and Jews

explanation.surface: Saying hello to someone from the Middle East while out in the park.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite is a famous national park in California, known for its granite cliffs.

clue.text: Wooden utensils, maybe — about ten boxes

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: About ten boxes of wooden spoons and bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: Treen is a collective term for small handmade wooden household objects such as bowls and spoons.

clue.text: Party animal

definitions.meaning: a ... is a ... party, a groom's night out before the wedding

explanation.surface: A party animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stag names both a male deer and the pre-wedding celebration held for a groom by his friends.

clue.text: Cleaners — 51 separately joining in game

indicators.note: the two letters of the number do not stay together, so one is set apart from the other
joining in a game means taking part inside it, so the number goes within the word

parts.note: charades is a party guessing game of miming
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Cleaners at number 51 split up to take part in a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining in' puts LI into CHARADES, and 'separately' parts the two letters so the I sits further along: CHAR-L-AD-I-ES. A charlady is an old British word for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Charladies were women employed to clean houses or offices, an old-fashioned term for domestic cleaners.

clue.text: Antagonise English eccentric

parts.note: an eccentric person is strange, odd

explanation.surface: Annoying an odd Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate someone, turning them hostile or unfriendly.

clue.text: Dramatist in France briefly flying east

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: racing means going very fast, flying along

explanation.surface: A playwright in France makes a quick dash eastwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was the great seventeenth-century French tragedian, author of Phèdre.
